title: safe2 assess --manifest: local project manifest and opt-in hosted post
outcome: A user can write a validated names/flags/counts/digests manifest locally and, only on explicit request, post it to the hosted assessment service.
acceptance_conditions: --manifest stops before any read, write or send unless --scan-content and --inspect-config are given.
Collection opens no network connection; --post is the only outbound request and takes its key from the environment only.
Collection that cannot read a file or construct unambiguously fails closed and writes no manifest.
The manifest validates against the vendored schema before it is written and carries no file contents, prompts, secret values, command lines or tool arguments.
Rollback is deleting the branch before merge, or reverting the merge commit after it.
trust_boundaries: customer project and user-level agent configuration files to the CLI (local reads)
CLI to hosted assessment endpoint over HTTPS (agent-to-tool plane, one opt-in POST)
SAFE2_MCP_PRO_KEY from the process environment to the one request
assumptions: This plan was produced retroactively, after the implementation, by the authoring agent (a bot); it is not a pre-implementation design record.
The only written design and threat model is safe2/docs/ASSESS-MANIFEST.md, drafted by the same agent.
unknowns: Whether the deployed hosted service accepts the generator name 'safe2 assess --manifest'.
Named human reviewer for manifest-heuristics-v1.json (status draft-unreviewed).
Whether an agent with no tools: line should be reported as inheriting built-in tools (see the PR 430 security-diff review, finding F2).

design.summary: A separate safe2/manifest package collects facts through the bounded reader and writes notes first and the manifest last; a post client makes one fixed-endpoint POST with no redirects.
